name: Cell Freezing
description: Cryopreservation of mammalian cells for long-term storage in liquid nitrogen. Use healthy, actively dividing cells at 70–80% confluency for best viability after thaw.
source_note: General educational template for mammalian cell cryopreservation.

steps.title: Prepare freezing medium
steps.description: Prepare fresh freezing medium: 90% complete culture medium + 10% DMSO (or use commercial CryoStor CS10). Keep on ice. Prepare enough for target number of vials (~1 mL per vial).
steps.notes: Prepare freezing medium fresh. Pre-chill on ice before adding to cells — DMSO generates heat on dilution.
steps.warnings: DMSO rapidly penetrates skin and carries dissolved compounds with it. Wear nitrile gloves and change immediately if contaminated.

steps.title: Harvest cells by trypsinization
steps.description: Trypsinize cells as per standard passaging protocol. Neutralize trypsin with complete medium, transfer to a conical tube, and centrifuge.
steps.notes: Use cells at 70–80% confluency for best viability after thaw.

steps.title: Count cells and assess viability
steps.description: Resuspend pellet in a small volume of medium. Count cells using hemocytometer + trypan blue or automated counter. Note total cell number and viability (should be >90%).

steps.title: Centrifuge cells
steps.description: Centrifuge counted cell suspension to pellet cells.

steps.title: Resuspend in ice-cold freezing medium
steps.description: Aspirate supernatant. Resuspend cell pellet in pre-chilled freezing medium to achieve the desired cell density (1–5 × 10⁶ cells/mL). Pipette gently — DMSO is toxic to warm cells.
steps.notes: Work quickly. DMSO toxicity increases with time and temperature.
steps.warnings: DMSO is toxic to cells at room temperature — keep cold and aliquot quickly.

steps.title: Aliquot into cryovials
steps.description: Quickly aliquot 1 mL per labeled cryovial. Tighten caps securely. Work on ice throughout.
steps.notes: Label vials with: cell line, passage number, date, initials, cell count.

steps.title: Place in controlled-rate freezing container and transfer to −80°C
steps.description: Place cryovials in a controlled-rate freezing container (e.g., Mr. Frosty filled with isopropanol, pre-chilled to RT). Transfer to −80°C freezer. This gives a −1°C/min cooling rate for optimal cryopreservation.

reagents.name: 100% isopropanol (for Mr. Frosty or equivalent)
reagents.notes: Pre-chill container at RT per manufacturer instructions

equipment: Controlled-rate freezing container (Mr. Frosty or equivalent)
steps.notes: Leave in −80°C overnight (minimum 4–6 h). The isopropanol jacket provides −1°C/min cooling rate.
steps.warnings: Replace isopropanol in Mr. Frosty after 3–5 freeze cycles.

steps.title: Transfer to liquid nitrogen for long-term storage
steps.description: Transfer vials from −80°C to liquid nitrogen storage (vapor or liquid phase) for long-term preservation. Update cell stock inventory/logbook.
steps.notes: Transfer within 24 h of placing in −80°C. Cells at −80°C lose viability over weeks. Update inventory database.
steps.warnings: Liquid nitrogen can cause cryogenic burns. Use cryogenic gloves, lab coat, and face shield. Ensure ventilated area.
